(a) The paragraph under the heading “general provisions” under the appropriations for the Post Office Department contained in chapter IV of the Supplemental Appropriation Act, 1951 (64 Stat. 1050), as amended by section 213 or the Postal Rate Increase Act, 1958 (72 Stat. 143; 31 U.S.C. 695), is repealed effective as of July 1, 1966. 
    (b) Section 207(b) of the Act of February 28, 1925 (43 Stat. 1067), as amended by section 7 of the Act of May 29, 1928 (45 Stat. 942), is repealed as of the effective date of the first section of this Act.

fable.w: This section only repeals earlier statutory provisions concerning Post Office Department appropriations and a 1925 Act. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. There is no tempting reading beyond the reference to postal rate legislation, which does not create any outside-party process.
fable.s: is repealed effective as of July 1, 1966.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of repealing existing statutory provisions. It does not establish any new process for consultation, public comment, advisory committees, or coordination with outside parties. Repealing a law is a legislative action that does not inherently involve participation by non-federal entities in a decision-making process.

opus.w: This section only repeals two earlier postal appropriation and statutory provisions and sets the dates those repeals take effect. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. The only tempting reading is that the cited postal rate laws concern the public, but repealing them involves no outside participation in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section solely repeals existing statutory provisions regarding appropriations and postal rates. It does not establish any new advisory committees, public comment periods, consultations with outside entities, or rights to sue. The text contains no language requiring or recommending interaction with parties outside the federal government for decision-making purposes.
qwen_chat.s:
(a) The paragraph under the heading “general provisions” under the appropriations for the Post Office Department contained in chapter IV of the Supplemental Appropriation Act, 1951 (64 Stat. 1050), as amended by section 213 or the Postal Rate Increase Act, 1958 (72 Stat. 143; 31 U.S.C. 695), is repealed effective as of July 1, 1966. 
    (b) Section 207(b) of the Act of February 28, 1925 (43 Stat. 1067), as amended by section 7 of the Act of May 29, 1928 (45 Stat. 942), is repealed as of the effective date of the first section of this Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that repealing a section could implicitly remove a participation requirement, or that the repealed sections contained participation mechanisms. However, the text provided only describes the repeal of specific statutory provisions and does not itself establish, require, or recommend any process for outside parties to participate in a federal decision. The definition requires the section *itself* to involve participation (e.g., consultation, hearings, advisory boards with non-federal members). Since this section is purely a repeal of existing law without creating new participatory mechanisms, it does not meet the definition.
